sections.h2: Which Edmonton offices run Metcalfe County property tax?
sections.html:
In Metcalfe County the PVA appraises, the sheriff mails the bill and takes the payment, and the county clerk inherits any bill left open in the spring. The county's own PVA site, hosted on qpublic.net, publishes the roll and a tax calendar.

Edmonton is the county seat and also its one incorporated city.

sections.h2: Where does Metcalfe County sit, and who buys homes there?
sections.html:
Metcalfe spreads over about 290 square miles of south central Kentucky. It was organized in May 1860 as the 106th Kentucky county and honors Thomas Metcalfe, governor from 1828 to 1832. The Glasgow micropolitan area includes it, and that area belongs to the Bowling Green and Glasgow combined statistical area. Wikipedia lists Summer Shade as a census designated place and Alone as a ghost town.

Edmonton sits on the Louis B. Nunn Cumberland Parkway. The county site puts Interstate 65 about 29 miles away by that road, Glasgow 16 miles west, Louisville 113 miles away, Lexington 124, and Nashville 112. U.S. 68 and Kentucky routes 80 and 163 also serve the town. CSX rail service is near Glasgow, and Moore Field there has a 4,586 foot paved runway.

Neighboring counties are Hart, Green, Adair, Cumberland, Monroe and Barren. Because the county sits inside the Glasgow area, a seller may meet buyers who work toward Glasgow or Bowling Green. The county site gives Edmonton about 1,586 residents in 2010, against 10,099 in the whole county, so most owners live outside the city. The 2020 census put the median age at 41.9 years, with 19.0 percent of residents 65 or older, which is the group that can claim the homestead exemption described below.

sections.h2: What does the Census Bureau report on Metcalfe County homes?
sections.html:
In 2020 the county had 10,286 residents, barely above 10,099 in 2010, and mid-2025 brought an estimate of 10,583. That 2020 tally showed 4,691 housing units with 11.6 percent standing empty, and the whole population lived in rural territory.

The five year survey reports:

  • Homeowners live in 77.7 percent of homes, the top rate among these four counties.
  • Housing costs for owners come to $1,066 a month with a mortgage and $368 with none.
  • Jobs numbered 1,234 in 2023, 7.5 percent fewer than the year before.
  • Commutes average 25.9 minutes, the briefest of the four.
  • Per capita income is $27,314, and 83.3 percent of households have a broadband subscription.

sections.h2: Which Metcalfe County offices handle tax questions?
sections.html:
The elected officials page lists these contacts.

  • Sheriff: bills and collections. P.O. Box 371, Edmonton, KY 42129, phone (270) 432-3041.
  • PVA: values, exemption forms, mailing address changes. P.O. Box 939, phone (270) 432-3162, and the site is www.qpublic.net/ky/metcalfe.
  • Fiscal Court: county government, with a street address of 201 North Main and a mailing box at P.O. Box 149, phone (270) 432-3181.
  • County Attorney: P.O. Box 999, phone (270) 432-0777.

Lien and delinquent bill details come from the county clerk's office. A new owner who never receives a bill should contact the sheriff, the PVA site advises.

sections.h2: Which payment dates apply in Metcalfe County?
sections.html:
KRS 134.015 ends the 2 percent discount on November 1. Yet the PVA's calendar page lists November 30 as the discount deadline, December 1 to 31 for the plain amount, and January 1 as the start of delinquency. Read the dates on your own bill, and confirm with the sheriff before you count on the later one.

The same calendar also shows:

  • September 15: the sheriff has the bills in hand.
  • January: 5 percent added.
  • February onward: 10 percent added, together with a 10 percent sheriff fee.
  • April 15, close of business: the bills pass from sheriff to clerk.
  • July 14 to August 28: window for the clerk's certificate sale, with the sheriff's settlement due September 1.

sections.h2: What steps lead to a Metcalfe County assessment appeal?
sections.html:
Start with the PVA while the roll is on public view, which runs 13 days from the first Monday of May and includes Saturdays. If the conference fails, go to the county clerk, and do it by the next workday after the viewing period closes.

The appeals board has three local members, named by the mayor of the county's largest city, the fiscal court and the judge executive. Since Edmonton is the only city, its mayor makes one of those picks. A change by the board must come with a written explanation, and you may record the hearing.

  • Sale prices and dates of similar homes near yours.
  • A contractor quote for repairs that the PVA record omits.
  • The dollar value you claim, written on the form.

If you file and then skip the hearing, you cannot take the appeal further.

sections.h2: How is rural land valued in Metcalfe County?
sections.html:
State rules send PVAs to every parcel at least every four years and put new buildings on the roll annually. Farm land can be assessed at what it is worth as agriculture instead of its fair cash value, the Department of Revenue says.

On nearly 290 square miles with about 10,500 residents, many Metcalfe County sales include acreage. If any part of a parcel is farmed, ask the PVA about its classification before you list.

sections.h2: Do Metcalfe County seniors get a homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Yes. An owner who turns 65 during the year, or is classified as totally disabled on January 1, applies at the PVA for the home they own and live in. KRS 132.810 allows a single exemption for each residential unit and includes mobile homes and manufactured houses.

A disabled owner under 65 reapplies yearly, except a service connected totally disabled veteran or a person with a permanent disability finding. Applying before payment reduces the bill, and applying afterward earns a refund.

sections.h2: What follows a missed Metcalfe County payment?
sections.html:
Unpaid bills reach the clerk's office at the end of April 15 as certificates of delinquency, each with a lien on record. Interest of 1 percent a month builds up, and clerk and county attorney fees (10 and 20 percent) follow. A public listing is required at least 30 days before the sale.

KRS 134.015 makes the January 1 owner personally liable, and the lien can trail the property for 11 years. A private buyer who gets the certificate collects from the owner and may add fees.

sections.h2: Does back tax stop a Metcalfe County sale?
sections.html:
It does not have to. The sheriff quotes the payoff before April 15 and the clerk afterward, and the amount grows monthly once the clerk has it. Request a written figure dated close to closing.

January 1 settles tax ownership, so a late year sale leaves the bill with the previous owner until next year. Many Metcalfe County sellers hold older houses with repairs put off. To weigh a cash offer against a listing, work out each net after repairs, tax and months of carrying cost.

faqs.q: Who takes payment of Metcalfe County property tax?
faqs.a: The county sheriff, whose mailing box is P.O. Box 371 in Edmonton. The listed number is (270) 432-3041.

faqs.q: Is there a city property tax in Edmonton?
faqs.a: Edmonton is the county's only incorporated city. Ask the Fiscal Court at (270) 432-3181 whether a city bill applies to your parcel.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Metcalfe County PVA?
faqs.a: Call (270) 432-3162 or write to P.O. Box 939, Edmonton, KY 42129. The office site is www.qpublic.net/ky/metcalfe.

faqs.q: When can a Metcalfe County owner contest a value?
faqs.a: During the 13 days that begin on the first Monday of May. A PVA conference has to come before any filing.

faqs.q: How long does a delinquent tax lien last?
faqs.a: Up to 11 years under KRS 134.015, through any change of owner.
